mechanism_narrative: The strong upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the last two weeks indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive retail and recreation mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in WORKPLACES mobility, crossing a threshold of -30% from baseline, signals a return to office work that will boost associated retail and recreation activities in the vicinity of workplaces over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES rising above -30% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests people are spending less time at home and more time out for essential activities, which will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL continues to fall and GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: Easing of public health policies encourages greater use of public transit, and the recent uptick in TRANSIT station visits reflects this policy shift, facilitating greater access to retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, indicating policy changes did not translate to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility crossing above its pre-pandemic baseline indicates a significant return to normal out-of-home activity for essential errands, which will encourage further non-essential retail and recreation visits over the next one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggests a return to urban centers for work, which will directly increase foot traffic to retail and recreation establishments located near transit hubs and workplaces over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite concurrent increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained shift away from staying at home, freeing up time and willingness for out-of-home activities including retail and recreation, driving an increase over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of increasing overall mobility, the recent sharp drop in PARKS visits suggests a shift from outdoor leisure to indoor or more structured retail and recreation activities, contributing to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility drops significantly week-on-week while other mobility categories rise
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days despite a significant drop in PARKS mobility.
